Rashi on Chullin 3b:11:1.hebrew: אביי ורבא ורב אשי לא מצו לתרוצי לעיל, וכולן דמתניתין:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:11:1.english: Abaye, Rava, and Rav Ashi could not resolve [the difficulty raised] above, and all of them [align] with our Mishnah.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:12:1.english: On the contrary, there it is primary - and he should not have taught it here.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:13:1.english: And that which it says - "since the tanna taught," etc. [i.e., this refers to the phrase "since the tanna taught the case of a ritually impure person slaughtering non-sacred animals, he teaches the case of sacrificial animals as well"].

Rashi on Chullin 3b:13:2.hebrew: לאו כקדש דמו - ואין חייב ליזהר בהו, ופשיטא דשוחטין טמאים לכתחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:13:2.english: Their [legal] status is not like that of sacred [food] - meaning, one is not obligated to be careful regarding them [i.e., to keep such non-sacred food prepared in purity from becoming impure], and it is obvious that ritually impure people may slaughter them [such animals] from the outset.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:14:1.english: They are experts - Therefore there is no need to examine him.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:1.english: Like the difficulty - that he [Abaye] raised it from [the case of] one who leaves a gentile alone in his shop.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:2.hebrew: ואביי לא אמר כרבא - דיליף מהשומר את החנות, דיוצא ונכנס לכתחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:2.english: And Abaye did not say like Rava - because he [Rava] derives [his ruling] from [the law of] one who watches a store, that it suffices for him to go out and come in, [and this applies] even ab initio.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:3.english: There, he did not touch [it] - [Meaning:] that idolater, with regard to the wine, [is referring to] the moment when he is moving away from it.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:4.hebrew: הכא - בהמה זו ביד הכותי נתונה, כהרף עין שוהה או דורס, הלכך לא סמכינן איוצא ונכנס:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:16:4.english: Here - this animal is placed in the hand of the Samaritan; in the blink of an eye he might pause [too long] or press [down improperly with the knife], therefore we do not rely on [the argument of] "he went out and came in."

Rashi on Chullin 3b:18:1.english: He does not hold like this [ruling] of Rava - who said that an apostate Jew may slaughter ab initio [if there is] an inspection of the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:18:2.english: Rather, [as for] Rava - [The Gemara raises this question] because he says that a Jewish apostate is permitted to slaughter ab initio by having his knife checked [beforehand].

Rashi on Chullin 3b:18:3.hebrew: אמאי לא אמר כשמעתיה - אמאי לא אוקמיה מתניתין בישראל מומר, ולכתחלה דקתני בבדק סכין, ודיעבד דקתני בשלא בדק, כדאוקמה רב אשי בתר שמעתיה דרבא:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:18:3.english: Why did he not say [it] according to his own teaching - Why did [Rava] not establish the Mishnah [as referring] to an apostate Israelite, with [the clause] "ab initio," which it teaches, [referring to a case] where the knife was examined, and [the clause] "after the fact," which it teaches, [referring to a case] where it was not examined - just as Rav Ashi established it, following Rava's own teaching?

Rashi on Chullin 3b:19:1.hebrew: לדבריו דאביי - דלא ס"ל הא דרבא, ואוקמה בכותי, ואוקי לכתחלה בישראל עומד על גביו, ואוקי דיעבד ביוצא ונכנס. ואמר ליה רבא: לדידך דלא סבירת לך במומר ומוקמת ליה הכי, אפילו ביוצא ונכנס מצית לאוקומי לכתחלה, ודיעבד אוקי בבא ומצאו ששחט:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:19:1.english: According to Abaye's words - [Rav Ashi says this] because he [Abaye] does not hold like this teaching of Rava's, and he [Abaye] establishes it [the Mishnah's "all may slaughter"] as referring to a Samaritan (Kuti), and he establishes the "ab initio" case [where the ruling is lenient only] when an Israelite stands over him, and he establishes the "after the fact" case as one who went out and came back in. And Rava said to him: "According to you, who do not hold like [the law of] an apostate and establish it this way, even in the case of 'went out and came back in' you can establish it as 'ab initio,' and for 'after the fact,' establish it as 'he came and found that [the Samaritan] had [already] slaughtered.'"

Rashi on Chullin 3b:1:1.english: If his knife is found to be flawless, it is permitted - This is [an instance of] the after-the-fact (bedieved) [ruling] of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:2:1.hebrew: חוץ מחש"ו דאפילו - נמצאת סכינו יפה לא, דאיכא קלקולא אחרינא: שהייה, דרסה, חלדה, דלא ידעי לאזדהורי בהו. ודוקא אוכל לתיאבון, אבל להכעיס, אפילו נמצאת סכינו יפה לא, דמועד לנבל בכוונה בידים:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:2:1.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, for even - [in their case,] even if his knife is found to be fine, [his slaughter] is not [valid], because there is another flaw [to worry about]: interrupting the slaughter, pressing the knife, or digging it in - since they do not know how to be careful about these. And this [leniency, of examining the knife after the fact] applies specifically to one who eats [forbidden food] out of appetite; but if he does so out of spite, even if his knife is found to be fine, [his slaughter] is not [valid], because he is presumed to invalidate it intentionally, with his own hands.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:3:1.english: May slaughter ab initio - Even if no others are watching him.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:3:2.english: Let him examine it now - Why do I need others to see [him examine it]? [He can simply examine it himself now, without witnesses.]

Rashi on Chullin 3b:3:3.english: What of it? - [Because] they [the onlookers] did not examine the knife.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:4:1.english: Experts - Meaning, they know the laws of ritual slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:4:2.english: And even though they are not established [as experts] - [meaning] that they have not slaughtered before us three times, to see whether they have the strength that they do not faint during slaughter - which would lead to a pause (shehiyah) - or [whether] they do not know how to train their hands for this.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:5:1.english: In what case is this said? - [Referring to a case] where they are considered qualified experts.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:5:2.hebrew: שיודעין בו - אלו המוסרים לו בהמה לשחוט, מכירין בו ובדקוהו שיודע הלכות שחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:5:2.english: That they know him - [This refers to] those who hand him an animal to slaughter: they know him and have examined him, that he knows the laws of slaughtering.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:6:1.hebrew: דאפי' דיעבד - ויודעין הלכות שחיטה לא, דתמיד הם מוחזקים לקלקל, שאין בהן דעת:
Rashi on Chullin 3b:6:1.english: That even after the fact - Even if they know the laws of ritual slaughter, [it does not help; their slaughter is still invalid], for they are always presumed liable to ruin [the slaughter], since they lack understanding (da'at).

Rashi on Chullin 3b:8:1.english: Established [muchzakim] - [Meaning] that we have seen them slaughter many times properly, without spoiling [the slaughter].

Rashi on Chullin 3b:8:2.english: Even though they are not experts - Because we do not know about them whether they know how to state the laws of slaughter or not.

Rashi on Chullin 3b:8:3.hebrew: נתעלף - לשון עייפות וחלישות הלב, שאין יכול לראות מכת חרב וסכין אפילו בבהמה, כמו תתעלפנה הבתולות (עמוס ח):
Rashi on Chullin 3b:8:3.english: Fainted - An expression of weariness and faintness of heart, that he cannot bear to see the blow of a sword or knife even on an animal, as in "the maidens shall faint" (Amos 8).

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:13:1.english: Non-sacred food that was prepared in the purity of consecrated food is not considered like consecrated food - This reason [the Gemara gives here, according to the latter version] could also have been said according to the first version (lishna kama).

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:14:1.hebrew: רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן - ושוחטין אף לכתחלה. אבל אין לפרש דדיעבד הוא דהויא שחיטתו כשרה, אע"פ שאין אחרים רואין אותו, ולא מצי לאוקומי מתניתין בהכי, משום דקשיא לן "וכולן", דהא לאביי ורבא ורב אשי לא מיתוקם נמי "וכולן" אלא אחרש שוטה וקטן:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:14:1.english: Most of those present at a slaughtering are experts - meaning that they may slaughter even ab initio (lechatchila). But one cannot explain this to mean that it is only after the fact (bediavad) that his slaughter is valid, even though others are not watching him, for one cannot establish the mishnah this way, because we find it difficult [to reconcile this reading] with [the clause] "and all of them" (ve-chulan) - for even according to Abaye, Rava, and Rav Ashi, "and all of them" cannot be established [to include a non-expert] either, but only [refers to] a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor (cheresh, shoteh, ve-katan).

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:17:1.hebrew: קסבר כותים גרי אריות הן - ושחיטתן פסולה, כמו של עובדי כוכבים. מ"וזבחת": "מה שאתה זובח אתה אוכל", כלומר אותו שהוא בר זביחה, לאפוקי עובד כוכבים ואוכל נבלות להכעיס. ואע"ג דאמר בסוף פ"ב דיבמות (דף כד:) "אחד גרי אריות ואחד גרי חלומות, כולם גרים גמורים" - היינו כשמתגייר לגמרי מפחד אריות, אבל כותיים לא נתגיירו לגמרי, כדכתיב במלכים (ב יז) "את ה' היו יראים ואת אלהיהם היו עובדים". ומאן דאמר גרי אמת הן, קסבר דשוב נתגיירו לגמרי:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:17:1.english: He holds that the Kutim are converts [out] of [fear of] lions - and their slaughter is invalid, like that of idol worshippers. From [the word] "vezavachta" ["and you shall slaughter"] [we derive]: "that which you slaughter, you [may] eat" - meaning, [the valid slaughterer is] one who is fit to eat from the slaughtering, excluding an idol worshipper, and [excluding] one who eats forbidden carcasses (neveilot) out of spite (le'hach'is). And even though it says at the end of the second chapter of Yevamot (24b): "both converts of lions and converts of dreams - they are all full converts" - that is referring to when one converts fully out of fear of lions, but the Kutim did not convert fully, as it is written in [the book of] Kings (II 17): "They feared the Lord, and they worshipped their gods." And the one who says they are converts in truth (geirei emet) holds that they later converted fully.

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:18:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא לא אמר כשמעתיה - תימה, דהא קתני במתניתין תרי הכל שוחטין, ומפרש רבא לקמן (חולין דף יז.) חדא לאתויי כותי וחדא לאתויי ישראל מומר, אלמא מוקי חדא כשמעתיה. וי"ל דהכי פריך: דקמייתא איבעי ליה לאוקומי כשמעתיה:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:18:1.english: What is the reason he did not say [a resolution] in accordance with his own view - This is difficult, for the mishna teaches "everyone may slaughter" twice, and Rava explains further on (Chullin 17a) that one [occurrence] comes to include a Samaritan (Kuthi), and one comes to include a Jewish apostate (yisrael mumar). This shows that he does establish one of them in accordance with his own view (keshmateta). And one can answer: this is indeed the question - that it is the first [occurrence] that he should have established in accordance with his own view.

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:1:1.hebrew: בודק סכין ונותן לו - ולא חיישינן שמא ישהה וידרוס, דלא שביק היתירא ואכיל איסורא, ואפילו לא יאכל ממנה, דחייש אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול, אפי' אין אחר עומד על גביו ולא יוצא ונכנס. אבל כותי יש לו דין אחר, דאי ישראל יוצא ונכנס לא בעי בדיקת סכין, דמרתת, דלא מצינו בשום מקום גבי כותי שיהא צריך בדיקת סכין. ואי אין ישראל יוצא ונכנס, אפי' בדק סכין לא מהני, דחיישינן שמא שהה ושמא דרס, דלא חייש אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול. ותימה, דאמאי לא מהני נמי במומר יוצא ונכנס כמו בכותי, דקאמר בסמוך אי דליתא לסכין כי אחרים רואין אותו מאי הוי. וי"ל דישראל מומר לא מירתת, דאין סבור שיבדקו הסכין אחריו, לפי שהוא מחזיק עצמו כישראל לכל דבריו. ואין להקשות דאמאי צריך לכתחלה לבדוק הסכין במומר ולהיות יוצא ונכנס, גבי כותי יניחנו לשחוט לכתחלה ואחרי כן יבדוק הסכין, או לכותי יתן כזית בשר. וי"ל דחיישינן דלמא משתלי ואכיל, כמו שפירש ר"ת גבי חרש שוטה וקטן דאין מוסרים להן חולין לכתחלה:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:1:1.english: He checks the knife and gives it to him - And we are not concerned that he [the apostate, mumar] will pause [in a way that invalidates the slaughter, shehiyah] or press down [invalidating it, derasah], for he would not forgo what is permitted to him and eat what is forbidden. And even if he himself will not eat from it, [we are still not concerned,] for he is [still] wary of [transgressing] "lifnei iver lo titein mikhshol" (do not place a stumbling block before the blind) [by giving out improperly-slaughtered meat that others may unknowingly eat] - even if no one else is standing over him, and there is no one going in and out [to check on him]. But a Cuthean (kuti) has a different law: for if a Jew is going in and out [checking on him], he does not need his knife checked, because he is fearful [of being caught] - for we do not find anywhere with regard to a Cuthean that his knife needs to be checked [when he is supervised in this way]. But if no Jew is going in and out, then even if he checked the knife, it does not help, for we are concerned lest he paused or pressed, since he is not wary of "lifnei iver lo titein mikhshol." Now, this is difficult: why doesn't [mere] going-in-and-out likewise suffice for an apostate, as it does for a Cuthean? For it says shortly [below]: if the knife is not there [to be checked] when others are watching him, what of it? [implying that supervision alone can substitute for a knife-check]. And one can answer that an apostate Jew is not fearful [of being caught], for he does not think anyone will check the knife after him, since he considers himself a [full-fledged] Jew in every respect [and so does not suspect that anyone doubts him enough to check up on him]. And one should not object [from the other side]: why is it necessary, ab initio (lechatchila), to check the knife for an apostate and also to have someone going in and out - [why not do] as with the Cuthean, [where one could] let him slaughter ab initio and check the knife afterward, or give him, like the Cuthean, [only] an olive's-bulk (kezayit) of meat [as a limited allowance]? For one can answer that we are concerned lest he forget and eat [before the meat has been verified fit] - just as Rabbeinu Tam explained with regard to a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor (cheresh, shoteh, ve-katan), that we do not hand over non-sacred food (chullin) to them ab initio.

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:5:1.hebrew: ואם שחט, בודקין אותו - ואע"ג דאיכא ברייתא לקמן (חולין דף יב.) דסבר דרוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן, גבי מצא תרנגולת שחוטה, הא מייתי תנאי בתר הכי, אע"ג דהתם דחי לה:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:5:1.english: And if he slaughtered, they examine him - And even though there is a Baraita further on (Chullin 12a) that holds that the majority of those found near slaughtering are experts, regarding [the case of] one who found a slaughtered chicken - [the Gemara] nevertheless cites tanna'im [who disagree] after that, even though there it rejects that view.

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:7:1.hebrew: דליתיה קמן דלבדקיה - תימה, דמשמע הא איתא קמן ולא ידע, אין שחיטתו כשרה, אע"ג דאחרים רואין אותו דשחט שפיר. ולקמן בפירקין (חולין דף יב.) גבי הא דאמר רב נחמן: ראה אחד ששחט, אם ראהו מתחלה ועד סוף מותר לאכול משחיטתו, ואם לאו אסור, פריך: אי דידע דלא גמיר פשיטא:
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:7:1.english: That he is not before us to examine him - This is astonishing, for it implies that if he is before us but we do not know [whether he is an expert], his slaughter is not valid, even though others see him slaughtering properly. But further on in this chapter (Chullin 12a), regarding what Rav Nachman says: if one saw someone slaughter - if he watched him from beginning to end, one may eat from his slaughter, and if not, it is forbidden - the Gemara asks: if [it means] that he knows [the slaughterer] is not learned [i.e., not an expert], that is obvious [that watching from start to end would not help]!

Tosafot on Chullin 3b:8:1.hebrew: אע"פ שאין מומחין - פירוש דלא ידעינן אי גמיר אי לא גמיר, דאי ידעינן ביה דלא גמיר, אפי' בדיעבד שחיטתו פסולה, כדאמר רב יהודה לקמן (חולין דף ט.): "כל טבח שאינו יודע הלכות שחיטה" כו':
Tosafot on Chullin 3b:8:1.english: Even though they are not experts - This means that we do not know whether he has learned [the laws of slaughter] or has not learned them. For if we knew of him that he had not learned them, then even after the fact (bediavad) his slaughter is invalid, as Rav Yehuda says further on (Chullin 9a): "Any slaughterer who does not know the laws of slaughter," etc. [it is forbidden to eat from his slaughter].
